_comment: The one file you tune per project (/harness-init writes the stack bits; harness.schema.json is the field reference). A project = one-or-more components, each with its own gate, plus a cross-cutting root gate.

models._comment: Per-phase {model, fallback, effort, fallbackEffort}: a Claude alias/ID; null = inherit session / no fallback. Fallback fires only on a FAILED invocation (unavailable or usage-limited). Enforced via settings.json `model`, agent frontmatter, and the loop dispatcher — /harness-doctor check 10 validates agreement. `effort` is DECLARED here and ENFORCED by settings.json `effortLevel` (session) + the phase agent's `effort:` frontmatter (subagents) — doctor check 10e validates both. Advisory by design: review/evaluate fallbackEffort (a usage-cap re-spawn pins the model, not the depth). The headless dispatcher passes --model only. IDS ARE PINNED, NOT ALIASES: the bare alias `opus` floats to the current Opus (now Opus 5), so `session` would silently become Opus 5 if written as `opus` — write the full ID for anything whose generation matters. Codex was removed from routing on 2026-08-11 (single-vendor by decision); the engine's codex arm still exists and is tested, it is simply unrouted. FALLBACKS ONLY ON THE FABLE PHASES (plan/review/evaluate), by decision 2026-08-11: Fable is the model that has actually usage-capped in practice (3x, killing reviews), and a headless run cannot ask a human for help mid-review. implement has NO fallback — if Opus 5 is capped the build simply stops, which is the honest outcome for an interactive phase. DOER != JUDGE: implement is Opus 5 and review is Fable 5, so the writer is never the reviewer. Residual edge, accepted knowingly — the review fallback IS Opus 5, so a Fable cap makes the reviewer the same model that wrote the diff. The primary guarantee still holds (the reviewer is a fresh context that never sees the conversation that produced the code); only model diversity is lost, only on a cap, and no diff merges without a human.

parallel._comment: Fleet runner: opt-in parallel workers over independent tasks (declared 'files' ownership), serialized merge queue. Review bandwidth binds before compute.

gate._comment: Cross-cutting gate, run from the repo ROOT after every component gate passes (usually just the e2e; all-null for a single-component project).

promotion._comment: Risk-gated promotion (/promote). Deterministic rules classify the diff first and can only RAISE the tier; a fresh-context risk-classifier agent then runs and can only raise it further. LOW may auto-approve + auto-merge to staging; MEDIUM/HIGH go to a human; anything matching alwaysHuman or moneySignals is HIGH unconditionally; prod is NEVER automated. Off by default — turn on deliberately, per docs/promotion.md.
